answer:
**Softmax must place its probability mass somewhere.** Some attention heads learn to allocate substantial weight to early tokens even when those tokens carry little obvious semantic information for the current query. These positions can act as attention sinks: stable places for excess or background attention mass rather than informative content retrieval. [1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.17453)

**Why a naive rolling cache can break behavior.** If training and early inference repeatedly included those initial positions, later attention patterns may rely on their presence. Evicting the oldest tokens removes the sinks along with old content, changing normalization and behavior even when the remaining recent context seems sufficient.

StreamingLLM retains a small set of initial sink positions together with a moving window of recent tokens. The cache stays bounded while preserving those special positions. This can stabilize streaming generation far beyond the original cache length without retaining every old token.

**Understand what is not preserved.** The model does not gain lossless memory of the entire conversation. Facts in evicted middle tokens are no longer directly available through that cache. “Infinite-length generation” means continuing the stream with bounded state, not accurately answering arbitrary questions about every event from an unlimited history.

Evaluate generation stability separately from long-term factual recall. The sink phenomenon also does not mean initial tokens are always meaningless: a system instruction at the beginning may have genuine semantic importance. Position-based sink behavior and content-based instruction following are distinct effects that can coexist.

**Technical details and references.**

Softmax must distribute total probability one, even when none of the visible tokens is especially useful. During training, initial tokens can become stable destinations for otherwise uninformative attention mass. Removing them at a sliding-window boundary changes the distribution the model expects. [1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.17453)

StreamingLLM retains a small initial-token cache plus a recent-token window. Cache memory is then $O((s+w)LH_{KV}d_h)$ rather than growing with the entire stream. The initial cache stabilizes attention while recent tokens carry local content.

This enables processing arbitrarily long streams with bounded cache, not remembering arbitrary facts from all past tokens. A fact evicted from the middle is unavailable unless encoded elsewhere. Test long-range recall separately from fluent continuation. Positional handling and the chosen sink/window sizes matter; the mechanism is not equivalent to simply increasing the trained context length.
